prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: I can’t objectively name a single “best” contractor for every situation — the right choice depends on your exact location in Miami, the roof type (shingle, tile, metal, single‑ply), whether you’re replacing after storm damage/insurance claim, and your budget. I can, however, tell you how to find the best hurricane‑rated roofer for your job and help produce a short vetted list if you give your ZIP code or let me look up local firms.

What to require for a hurricane‑rated roof replacement
- Miami‑Dade and Florida code compliance: materials and installation must meet Florida Building Code and Miami‑Dade County HVHZ requirements. Ask for Miami‑Dade Product Approval (NOA) numbers for the products used.  
- Proper contractor licensing and insurance: verify the contractor’s Florida license and that they carry General Liability and Workers’ Comp. Check DBPR (Florida Dept. of Business & Professional Regulation).  
- Manufacturer certifications: look for GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred, CertainTeed Select, Carlisle, Firestone or similar manufacturer-authorized installers — these provide stronger manufacturer warranties.  
- Wind rating / impact resistance: request systems rated for 130+ mph or whatever wind speed your locale requires, and Class 4 impact ratings if you want hail/impact protection.  
- Warranties: get both a manufacturer’s warranty and a written contractor workmanship warranty (duration and what it covers). Prefer a transferable warranty if you might sell the house.  
- Permits and inspections: contractor should obtain permits and schedule required inspections; don’t accept “no permit” work.  
- Local experience with hurricane mitigation: ask for recent hurricane‑rated installations and local references.  

Checklist of questions to ask every roofing contractor
- Are you licensed in Florida? What is your license number? (verify at DBPR)  
- Do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Can you provide certificates?  
- Do you have Miami‑Dade NOAs for the products and the installation method you’ll use?  
- Are you a certified installer for the roof system/manufacturer? Which one(s)?  
- Can you provide 3 local references for similar hurricane‑rated jobs completed in the last 2 years?  
- Who pulls the permit and schedules inspections? Will I receive lien waivers?  
- What warranties are included (manufacturer + workmanship) and are they transferable?  
- What is the projected timeline and cleanup policy?  

Where to verify and research contractors
- Florida DBPR license search (verify license status)  
- Miami‑Dade County product approvals / NOA database (verify materials)  
- BBB, Google Reviews, Houzz, Angi for real customer feedback  
- Local building department for permit history on recent jobs  

Typical best choices (by roof type)
- Asphalt shingle: choose a certified installer (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) with wind-rated, high‑uplift installation and Miami‑Dade approvals.  
- Tile: ensure proper fastening, underlayment and hurricane straps; use a roofer experienced with tile in HVHZ.  
- Metal: standing seam metal systems perform very well for high winds if installed per manufacturer/Miami‑Dade specs.  
- Flat/low‑slope (TPO/EPDM/PVC): pick commercial roofing specialists (Carlisle, Firestone) with local HVHZ experience.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated hurricane‑rated roofing contractors near your address or ZIP code and return a 3–5 contractor shortlist (with licenses, certifications, review summaries, and contact links).  
- Provide a printable contractor interview checklist and sample contract clauses to insist on.

Tell me your ZIP code and whether this is an insurance claim or private job and I’ll put together a short, localized list.
